correctness.rationale: Birkhoff support unions force at least five positive cells and exactly two supporting permutations when five are present. The unique primitive support orbit yields the displayed family. Direct characteristic factorization, branch derivatives and a 2x2 nilpotent Jordan reduction establish the unique parameter and global optimum. Standalone exact SymPy checks passed 9 possible five-cell supports, 6 primitive supports, 7 Jordan powers and 25 rational eigenvalue comparisons. Infinite claims follow from analytic arguments rather than finite samples.

originality.rationale: Compared exact statements and implications with the 2026 primitive-matrix paper and full text of the nearest public small-dimensional spectral and Birkhoff records. The published three-transposition return is in fact isospectral to the cube of the sparse kernel: its radical and exceptional-point mechanism are prior spectral coverage, not new. The dimension-three Birkhoff result classifies decomposition length. The separate global optimum over the complete minimum-positive-transition support class is not established by either prior theorem. No inspected result supplies the global minimal five-transition mixing optimum, though older equivalent Markov calculations remain a documented priority risk.

value.rationale: The smallest possible transition budget for an ergodic uniform three-state chain is a natural, complete constrained design class. The theorem supplies the sharp attainable per-step asymptotic mixing rate, the unique optimizer and a warning that the optimal chain is necessarily nonnormal with a generic polynomial transient. These are structurally informative resource-versus-mixing facts rather than an arbitrary finite substitution or a borrowed spectral table.
